Lesson 1: Car Accidents 
Have you ever been in a car accident? In today’s lesson, you’re going to learn 
expressions for describing different types of accidents, their causes, and 
results. 
Let’s begin with the difference between a car accident and a car crash. Car 
accident is the most general term – it can describe any type of accident, major 
or minor, and it can involve only one car or two or more cars.  
A car crash involves a collision – when a car hits an object with a violent 
impact. We can also use “crash” as a verb – for example, the car crashed into a 
tree, or the car crashed into a telephone pole. 
Here are four specific types of accidents: 
• When two vehicles crash into each other while traveling in opposite 
directions, we call this a head-on collision. This is one of the deadliest 
types of accidents.  
 
• On the other end of the spectrum is a fender-bender. This describes a 
small accident with very minor damage to the cars involved. 
• When multiple cars hit each other, this is called a pile-up. Pile-ups often 
occur when the weather and road conditions are bad. 
 
• Sometimes a car hits a person, but instead of stopping, the driver of the 
car drives away. This type of accident is called a hit and run. 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
Now we’ll look at four descriptions of accidents, and learn the verbs used for 
talking about them. 
#1 – I slammed on the brakes to avoid running over a dog. 
To slam on the brakes means to try to stop the car very suddenly, often 
in an emergency. In this case, the driver wanted to avoid running over 
a dog – the phrasal verb run over is used when a car passes over an 
object, animal, or person. 
#2 – The taxi sideswiped a parked car and then rear-ended a van. 
Sideswiped means the taxi hit the side of the parked car while passing 
it. Rear-ended means the taxi hit the back of the van. 
 
#3 – The driver lost control of the car and plowed into the guardrail. 
Inexperienced drivers can lose control of the car, especially when 
driving at high speeds, at night, or in bad weather. The phrasal verb 
plowed into is an alternative way to say crashed into. 
 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
#4 – Lots of cars were skidding on the icy road, and I saw one that had rolled 
over. 
The verb skid means to slide without control on a slippery surface like 
ice. If a car rolls over, that means it turns upside down. 
Car accidents can be caused by a number of factors. Here are some of the most 
common. 
• speeding – driving faster than the speed limit 
• tailgating – this is when one car drives extremely close behind another 
car. It’s dangerous because if the first car stops suddenly, the second car 
will not have time to stop. 
• drunk driving – driving under the influence of alcohol. To test for the 
level of alcohol in a driver’s blood, police use a breathalyzer test. 
• weather conditions – rain, snow, and ice can make the road slick or 
slippery. There can also be poor visibility (difficulty seeing) due to fog 
or darkness 
• reckless driving – the word reckless means “not careful” – so “reckless 
driving” means driving dangerously, not carefully – for example, people 
who change lanes without using the turn signal, or who drive 
impatiently and without careful observation or consideration 
• road rage – when a driver gets angry at another driver, and begins 
driving aggressively 
• distractions – when the driver is paying attention to other things – for 
example, their cell phone – and not watching the road. 
Finally, let’s look at the results of an accident. 
We can say the car is damaged and the people in the cars are injured or 
killed. A more formal word for someone killed in an accident is a fatality – for 
example, “there were three fatalities” or “luckily, there were no fatalities.” 
One common injury in car accidents is whiplash – an injury to the neck due to 
the sudden impact; when your head goes forward or backwards very 
suddenly. If someone in the car wasn’t wearing a seatbelt, they could be 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
thrown from the vehicle – this means they flew out of the vehicle and landed 
some distance away. 
When a car is badly damaged so that it can’t be driven, then it needs to be 
towed – transported by another vehicle, which is called a tow truck. (Your 
car can also be towed if you park in a prohibited area).  
 
A car being towed by a tow truck 
There’s a special word for when the car is damaged so badly it can’t be 
repaired – we say the car is totaled. 
Finally, if the occupants of the car were shaken but unhurt, it means that 
they were emotionally agitated (shaken), but they had no injuries (unhurt). 
You’ve finished Lesson 1! Now do the exercises accompanying this lesson to 
practice the vocabulary you’ve learned.

Lesson 2 – Personal Finance 
Today you’re going to learn some more advanced vocabulary for talking about 
money – from earning income to spending and managing your finances. 
Income & Assets 
The total amount of money you earn is called your income. Your income 
includes (but is not limited to) your salary (money you earn from your job). 
There are many other sources of income that don’t come directly from a job – 
for example: 
• dividends – money earned from investing in the stock market. 
• rental income – money you earn from renting out property to tenants 
(the people who rent and live in the house/apartment). 
• A pension – money you receive in regular, fixed payments after retiring.  
• welfare – money given to poor or disabled people by the government. 
Depending on your level of income, you’ll have to pay taxes – money you pay 
to the government for the maintenance of the country’s infrastructure, 
defense, social programs, etc. When you send in the document declaring your 
income and calculating your taxes, that is called filing your tax return. 
The total amount of wealth you possess – including all your money, your 
house and any other properties you own, your car and possessions – is called 
your assets. 
When people die, they usually leave their assets to their children or other 
relatives by means of a will – that’s the official document saying how the 
estate (another word for the total set of assets) should be distributed. The 
recipients are called heirs and the verb used is inherit – for example, “I 
inherited a house from my grandmother.” 
There are many different ways to say someone is rich or poor in English. The 
most common synonyms for “rich” are wealthy, well-off, and affluent. 
Alternative ways to say “poor” include needy, destitute, and impoverished.  


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
However, we also have some expressions referring to poverty that are more 
polite and indirect: 
• A working-class neighborhood 
• A blue-collar family 
• A low-income household 
Some people hope to get rich through a windfall – that means receiving a 
large amount of money suddenly and unexpectedly. For example, inheriting a 
lot of money from a relative who has died, or by winning the lottery or 
gambling – playing games based on luck, such as slot machines. The place 
where you can gamble is called a casino.  
 
Spending and Saving 
Some people never save money – instead, they live paycheck-to-paycheck. In 
other words, after they receive their salary, they spend it all – and then need 
to wait for the next paycheck. This is also called living hand-to-mouth. 
When a person is having difficulty surviving at their current level of income, 
we can say they’re scraping by or barely making ends meet. “Making ends 
meet” is an expression that means managing to survive with little money. 
Many families fall into the temptation of keeping up with the Joneses – this 
is when people try to accompany the standard of living of their friends, 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
colleagues or neighbors – for example, when your neighbor buys a new car, 
you feel the pressure to buy a new car of the same level.  
When you overspend – for example, you spent $10,000 on your credit card, 
but you can only pay $3,000 of it now – then you have a $7,000 debt. The 
word debt refers to money you owe – you borrowed it and used it, and now 
you need to pay it back. 
In addition to credit card debt, many people have debt from student loans 
(money you borrow to get a college education) and a mortgage (a loan you 
take out to buy a house). 
People who consistently spend more than they earn are “living beyond their 
means.” The opposite of that is “living within your means” – spending less 
than you earn.  
 
One way to live within your means and avoid spending too much is to make a 
budget – this is an organized plan for how much to spend in various 
categories like rent, food, gas, entertainment, etc.  
Your budget should include regular contributions to a savings account; 
financial advisers suggest having an emergency fund of three to six months’ 
living expenses saved up. 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
Finally, two more things you can do with your money are invest it in the stock 
market (in companies in the general economy) or make a donation to charity 
(non-profit organizations that help people, animals, or the environment). 
 
You’ve finished Lesson 2! Now continue to the exercises to practice the 
vocabulary you’ve learned.

Lesson 3: Health 
Today’s lesson covers a wide variety of health problems and their treatments. 
We’re going to go through the different systems of the human body one by 
one, studying the most common diseases and injuries that affect each of them. 
Skin 
Let’s start with several common problems affecting the skin: 
• A burn is an injury from heat or fire. Burns are classified into first-
degree, second-degree, and third-degree burns – from less serious to 
more serious. 
• A bruise is a blue, purple, or black area on the skin due to an impact. 
When this area is around the eye, we call this a “black eye.” 
 
a bruise 
• A cut is a break in the skin, usually accompanied by bleeding (when 
blood comes out of the body). If you are bleeding, you should keep 
pressure on the wound until the blood clots – hardens. A serious cut 
may require stitches – and it may leave a scar – a permanent mark on 
the skin. 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
 
stitches 
• A rash is an usual pattern of discoloration (often red or white) which 
can be caused by an allergic reaction or a disease. It may be itchy. 
 
Circulatory System 
Your circulatory system consists of your heart 
and blood vessels – arteries, which take blood 
away from the heart/lungs and transport it to 
the other parts of your body; and veins, which 
take blood back to the heart/lungs. 
One extremely common health problem in the 
world today is high blood pressure – when the 
pressure of the blood flow is elevated. Another 
common problem is high cholesterol – 
excessive fat in the blood. This can lead to a 
heart attack – when blood stops flowing to part 
of the heart, due to a blockage in one of the arteries. 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
If someone’s heart stops beating, one emergency treatment is to use a 
machine called a defibrillator, which gives the heart an electric shock. If no 
defibrillator is available, someone can perform CPR in order to keep blood 
flowing through the person’s body. 
 
Demonstration of CPR 
Brain & Nervous System 
Your skull protects your brain – but if you hit your head very hard, you’ll have 
a concussion, a minor injury to the brain due to impact. This may cause you 
to lose consciousness. Two more common expressions for “lose 
consciousness” are “faint” and “pass out.” 
 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
The major nerve that runs down the center of your back is called your spinal 
cord. Injuries to the spinal cord can result in a person being paralyzed – 
unable to move or feel parts of their body. 
Problems in the brain that result in changes to a person’s mood, behavior, 
and/or personality are known as mental illness. This is a general category 
that includes depression, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and other diseases. 
Internal Organs 
The number of problems that can affect the internal organs is huge, so let’s 
focus on two of the most common: diabetes and cancer. 
Diabetes results when the pancreas does not produce enough insulin – that’s 
a chemical that helps your body process sugar. A person who has diabetes is 
called diabetic, and they must carefully watch their diet and measure their 
blood sugar regularly. 
Cancer is a growth of abnormal cells in a part of the body. There are many 
different types of cancer – some of them are known by the part of the body 
affected (lung cancer, breast cancer, skin cancer) – and others have special 
names (leukemia – a cancer of the blood). 
A mass of abnormal cells is called a tumor. When a tumor is found, it must be 
biopsied (analyzed) to discover if it is benign (meaning it is not cancer) or 
malignant (meaning it IS cancer). Typical treatments for cancer include 
surgery to remove the tumor, radiation therapy, and chemotherapy (use of 
very powerful medications). 
Finally, if an internal organ is diseased or damaged beyond repair, a person 
may receive a transplant – an organ from another person (the one who gives 
the organ is called the donor; the one who receives the organ is called the 
recipient).  


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
Muscles & Joints 
Have you ever had one of these three injuries? They’re very common in 
sports: 
• A fracture is a broken bone. It can be diagnosed by X-ray, and the 
treatment is usually to immobilize the affected part of the body with a 
cast. 
 
a leg cast 
• A sprain is an injury to a joint; a ligament is over-extended or torn. 
• A strain or pulled muscle occurs when a muscle is over-extended or 
torn. 
If one of a person’s limbs is so badly damaged or diseased that it threatens the 
person’s health, doctors may have to amputate – remove – the affected arm, 
leg, hand, foot, finger, or toe. People who have undergone this process are 
known as amputees. Sometimes, they can begin using a prosthetic limb (an 
artificial arm/leg/etc.) to replace the body part that was lost. 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
 
An amputee with a prosthetic arm 
As people age, they are prone to develop arthritis – which results in soreness 
and stiffness (immobility) in the joints – and osteoporosis, a weakening of 
the bones which results in easy fractures. 
STDs – Sexually Transmitted Diseases 
A disease that can pass from one person to another is called contagious. Some 
diseases are spread by unprotected sexual relations. A few of these can be 
cured (eliminated) with antibiotics (medications that kill bacteria). 
Others, such as HIV/AIDS, do not yet have a cure – but the symptoms (the 
visible effects of the disease) can be managed by medication. If a patient is 
diagnosed early and takes all the meds, the prognosis (expectation for future 
health) is good. 
You’ve finished Lesson 3! Now continue to the exercises to practice the 
vocabulary you’ve learned. 
 
 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net

Lesson 4: Cooking 
In today’s lesson, you’re going to learn dozens of different verbs used in 
cooking and preparing food.  
We’ll begin with the differences between cuisine, dish, and specialty. The 
word “cuisine” refers to the general category of foods from a particular 
country or tradition – Japanese cuisine, Italian cuisine, Jewish cuisine. 
The word “dish” refers to a specific type of food within a cuisine – Italian 
cuisine includes various pasta dishes – spaghetti is one dish, lasagna is 
another dish, etc. 
The word “specialty” refers to a dish that is especially popular or typical in a 
restaurant or region. For example, you can have a restaurant that serves 
Brazilian cuisine, which offers various seafood dishes, and its specialty is 
shrimp stew. 
Let’s learn measurements used in cooking. If you’re following a recipe from 
the United States, you’ll find that things are measured using a different 
system: 
• cup = 237 ml 
• teaspoon = 5 ml 
• tablespoon = 15 ml 
• pound = 454 grams 
• ounce (used for solids) = 28 grams 
• fluid ounce (fl. oz. – used for liquids) = 30 ml 
Sometimes a recipe will also tell you to add a “pinch” or a “dash” of an 
ingredient. These words simply mean a small amount. The word “pinch” 
refers to the quantity you can take in two or three fingers, and it’s usually 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
used for solid seasonings – a pinch of salt, a pinch of pepper. The word “dash” 
refers to a small amount of a liquid – a dash of soy sauce, a dash of olive oil. 
Cutting Actions 
There are many different ways to cut something in the English language: 
• slice = cut into thin pieces 
 
• chop = cut something into square pieces 
• dice = cut something into smaller square pieces 
• mince = cut something into extremely small pieces – as small as you can 
 
• grate = make small fragments of something by rubbing it against a 
surface such as a grater. We usually grate cheese. 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
 
• peel = remove the skin from a fruit or vegetable 
 
• mash/crush = press something with force; ex. mashed potatoes 
 
 
Seasoning & Mixing Actions 
After all the ingredients are ready, it’s time to put them together. The verbs 
typically used for mixing are: 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
• mix/combine = put two or more things together 
• blend/puree = mix ingredients very well using a blender 
 
• stir = to mix something using a spoon 
• knead = this verb is used specifically for dough for bread, cakes, 
cookies, and so on. It refers to folding, pressing, and stretching the 
dough with your hands. 
 
The word “seasoning” refers to adding spices for flavor. Sometimes we let 
meat or vegetables sit in a mixture of flavorful liquids for several hours before 
cooking – this is called marinating. If a recipe tells you to season or add salt 
“to taste,” it means add as much or as little as you like. 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
 
spices 
Heating/Cooling Actions 
Some recipes tell you to pre-heat the oven – that means you need to turn the 
oven on about 15 minutes before you plan to put the food in. 
 
• bake / roast = cook something inside the oven. We typically use “bake” 
for things like bread, cakes, and muffins, and “roast” for meat and 
vegetables 
 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
• boil = cook something in very hot water. We boil pasta. After it is 
finished cooking, you need to drain the pasta to remove the water. 
 
• steam = cook something ABOVE very hot water; it’s the water vapor 
that cooks the food. Vegetables are often steamed. 
• fry = cook something in oil 
 
• sauté = cook something in a very small amount of oil or butter 
• simmer = cook something on the stove on very low heat. Some recipes 
tell you to simmer with the pot or pan either “covered” or “uncovered.” 
What about some verbs for making something cold? 
• let cool = stop heating the food and let the temperature drop naturally 
• chill = put something in the refrigerator 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
• freeze = put something in the freezer 
When you take something – such as chicken – out of the freezer and let it 
warm up to room temperature, this is called thawing or defrosting the 
chicken. And when you heat something solid – like butter or cheese – so that it 
becomes liquid, this is called melting the butter or cheese. 
 
Finishing Actions 
As a final step, you can drizzle, dust, or sprinkle an ingredient onto the 
finished dish. All of these words mean to add a very small amount of 
something on top of the food. 
 
Drizzle is used for liquids – drizzle chocolate syrup over an ice cream sundae. 
Dust is used for tiny particles, such as sugar and cinnamon. Sprinkle is used 
for small pieces of something – sprinkle bits of bacon on a salad. 
And of course, when you bring the food to the table, you are serving it.

Lesson 5: Taking Care of Your Home 
You already know the words “house” and “apartment” – but here are a few 
more descriptive words for different types of residences. 
• A mansion is a very large house, usually occupied by rich people. This 
can also be called a manor if it is surrounded by a large area of land that 
belongs to the owners. 
 
• Trailers or RVs are large vehicles that can be used as homes (especially 
while traveling). 
 
• A farm is a piece of property with agricultural activity and/or animals. 
The house where people live is called the farmhouse, and the place 
where the animals live or the food is stored is called the barn. 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
 
 
farm  
 
 
 
 
barn 
• College students live in a dormitory (or “dorm” for short). 
• Members of the military live in large buildings called barracks and their 
individual living space is called their quarters. (These words are always 
plural, even when referring to only one unit). 
• A cabin or cottage is a small house located in the countryside or on the 
beach. 
 
• A hut is a small, simple house made of natural or primitive materials. It 
often has just one room. 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
 
• A shack is a badly-constructed house, usually occupied by poor people. 
Shacks are common in the slums – poor, heavily-populated urban areas. 
 
Cleaning the Home 
Let’s do a nice thorough cleaning. The first step is to declutter - this word 
means to simplify or eliminate clutter. What’s clutter? Clutter is extra objects 
that fill your house or your life, which you don’t really need, or don’t use 
frequently. 
 
This is clutter! 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
Next we’ll use a rag or cloth to polish the furniture. The word “polish” 
means to make something shiny. You can polish wood or metal. 
 
Let’s also do the laundry – that means washing your clothes. We’ll need 
laundry detergent (the soap that washes the clothes), fabric softener to 
make the clothes soft and flexible, and bleach to remove stains (undesired 
marks) from white clothing. 
 
a stain on a white shirt 
If you don’t have a dryer… you’ll need to hang your clean clothes on a 
clothesline using clothespins. 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
 
clothesline and clothespins 
Now we’ll sweep the floor using a broom and dustpan. After sweeping, you 
can mop the floor with a mop and bucket. And if you have carpeted floors, 
you’ll need to vacuum with a vacuum cleaner.

vacuum cleaner 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
Time to take on the bathroom. You can use a sponge for light cleaning, and a 
brush for scrubbing – that means rubbing something very intensely to clean 
it. If your bathroom has tiles, you might need to use a special product to 
eliminate the mold (fungus) between them. 
 
 
sponge and brush  
 
 
 
tiles 
 
Home Repairs 
Are you handy? Describing someone as “handy” means they have skills in 
working with their hands, and they can fix various things. If not, you’ll need to 
call a professional! 
Let’s say your toilet is clogged (blocked). You can try to fix it yourself with a 
plunger, but if that doesn’t work, you can call a plumber – someone who 
specializes in working with water systems and pipes.  
 
 
 
plunger 
 
 
 
 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
The plumber can also help you if there’s a leak in your pipes – meaning water 
is coming out where it’s not supposed to – or if a pipe bursts – explodes due 
to excess internal pressure. 
If your house is infested with insects or rats, you’ll need a pest control 
service or exterminator to get rid of them. 
An electrician can handle problems with the wiring or the light fixtures.  
 
If you accidentally lock yourself out of your house, you'll need to call a 
locksmith. And when a large household appliance breaks, such as the 
refrigerator, water heater, or washing machine, a repairperson can go to 
your house and fix it. 
When you do extensive work to improve a house (or a room), such as 
knocking down walls, rebuilding, and changing the structure, this is called 
remodeling or renovation.

• http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_repair 
• http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_improvement

Lesson 6: Work & Employment 
Daily Work Routines 
Someone who works regular business hours has a nine-to-five job. Other 
people – such as bus drivers, emergency room doctors, waiters, and security 
personnel – work shifts, meaning they work for a certain period and then are 
replaced by another person who takes over the work.  
 
Example of shifts 
Some employers also offer flex-time (a flexible schedule in which the 
employee can decide when to work). 
If you need to take a day off due to health reasons, that’s called taking a sick 
day. And pregnant women can take maternity leave – time off to have a baby. 
If you work outside your home, then you begin the day with your commute – 
this word refers specifically to the trip between your home and your place of 
employment. It can be used as either a noun or a verb. 
Thanks to technology, nowadays some people can telecommute or work 
remotely – meaning they work from home or another place using the phone 
and internet. 
 
Working remotely from a cafe 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
A profession which involves physical work is called manual labor. Farmers, 
mechanics, and construction workers perform manual labor.  
 
On the other hand, if you work primarily at a desk then you have a desk job. 
Some people with desk jobs work in small compartments called cubicles, and 
others have their own private rooms, called offices. 
 
cubicles 
People & Hierarchy 
The people you work with are called your colleagues or co-workers. 
Hopefully you have a good rapport with your colleagues – that means a good 
relationship in which you trust, respect, and like each other. (The “T” in 
rapport is silent). 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
Let’s talk about the company hierarchy – the order of power and 
responsibility. The person directly above you, who is responsible for 
observing your work, is your boss or supervisor – and the people below you 
are your subordinates. 
Some bosses have the annoying habit of micromanaging their subordinates. 
That means monitoring and interfering with every single detail of the 
subordinate’s work, without letting them work independently. 
Many companies do an annual performance review of their staff – an 
evaluation of each employee’s work and results every year. These 
performance reviews are often the basis for giving promotions (increase in 
power/responsibility) and raises (increase in salary). 
Employment Conditions 
Many countries have a minimum wage – the minimum salary that companies 
are required to pay employees. Sometimes, in order to avoid paying the 
minimum wage, companies hire people to work “under the table” – that 
expression means the person is not legally/officially employed. 
Unfortunately, there’s still a lot of inequality in the job market, such as 
discrimination (different treatment of people) on the basis of skin color. In 
some professions, there is a “glass ceiling” – meaning an invisible barrier that 
prevents women and/or minorities from advancing to high positions. 
If the employees feel they are overworked (required to work too much) and 
underpaid (not paid enough), they might go on strike. “Going on strike” 
means they stop working until the company agrees to give them better 
working conditions. In many countries, each profession has an organization 
called a union which supports workers’ rights and negotiates with the 
company leadership during a strike. 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
 
workers on strike 
To avoid a strike, employers can provide incentives for good performance and 
make sure that morale – the general feeling/spirit of the group – stays high. 
Some companies offer their staff nice perks (that’s an informal word for 
“benefits”) such as a car or cell phone paid for by the company. 
A job is not only a way to earn a living (get money for daily life), but it can 
also be rewarding (meaning it gives satisfaction). If you have a job that you 
love or you have wanted to do for a long time, and/or which has great 
benefits, that’s called a dream job.

Lesson 7: Issues in Education 
Let’s begin by reviewing the different levels and types of education. 
• Primary education refers to the first 5-7 years of schooling. This 
includes elementary school and middle school. 
 
• Secondary education is what we call high school in the U.S. – it is the 
school attended during adolescence. 
 
• Higher education refers to college and university. This includes 
undergraduate studies (typically four years) and graduate studies 
(Master’s and Doctorate programs). 
Parents can choose to send their children to a public school, which is run by 
the government, or a private school, which is run by a company or 
institution. 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
One alternative form of education is homeschooling – where the parents 
teach their children at home. And special education is for children with 
disabilities and special needs. 
Classroom Management 
Teachers must deal with a number of difficult issues in the classroom. 
Students may cheat – get the answers in a dishonest way – in order to get 
good grades. Examples of cheating include looking at another student’s test 
and using a cell phone to find answers during an exam. 
Another form of cheating is plagiarism, when a student copies someone else’s 
written work and claims it as his own. (“Plagiarism” is the noun, and 
“plagiarize” is the verb). 
Here are three common punishments given to students for bad behavior in the 
U.S.: 
• If a student gets detention, it means he or she must stay at school after 
the regular hours. 
• If a student is suspended, it means he or she is not permitted to enter 
the school for a few days or weeks. 
• If a student is expelled, it means he or she is officially and permanently 
removed from the school. 
It’s not easy to be a teacher – but being a student also has its own share of 
difficulties. Students face peer pressure – influence from friends and 
classmates to act or think in a certain way. 
The popular kids at school can form a clique – a 
small and exclusive group of friends that often 
views itself as superior. The unpopular kids may be 
bullied – suffering abuse or threats. Bullying can be 
physical, verbal, emotional, or online (called “cyber 
bullying”). 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
Curriculum & Evaluation Issues 
One controversy in education today is regarding the use of standardized 
testing – tests that are given to all students in a region or country. 
Some people say this is essential for evaluating students and comparing 
school rankings (positions in a list of best to worst) – and others claim the 
use of such tests encourages students to focus on memorization and not 
develop critical thinking skills. 
Another debate involves whether or not fine arts 
(music, theater, dance, painting, etc.) should be 
included in the core curriculum – the essential 
and required set of courses – or whether they 
should be electives (optional courses) or 
extracurricular activities (done outside regular 
school hours). 
Finally, a current concern in the U.S. is regarding 
the incredibly high tuition (the price you pay for 
attending a private school) at many colleges and universities. Students who 
are unable to get scholarships (financial help for paying for studies) often 
take out large loans in order to attend elite schools (those which are 
considered superior) – then graduate with thousands of dollars in debt and 
are unable to find high-paying jobs in their areas. 
This is causing some students to choose different options like 
entrepreneurship (starting your own business) or entering a trade (manual 
work for which you need specialized skills/training, such as being a carpenter 
or mechanic).

Lesson 8: Socializing 
Specific Types of Social Events 
There are many different kinds of social events with specific names in English. 
Here are a few of the most common. 
When people move into a new house, they can have a housewarming party – 
an informal gathering in which the hosts (the people organizing the party) 
present their new home, and the guests (the people attending the party) give 
gifts of household items. 
When someone is moving away or leaving for a long trip like a semester or 
year abroad, their friends often organize a going-away party or send-off to 
say goodbye and wish them a good trip. 
Before getting married, some men have a bachelor party with their male 
friends to celebrate their “last day of freedom” as a single person. The female 
equivalent is a bachelorette party. Sometimes these parties are held at a 
strip club or bar, and other times they are more innocent. 
 
The word “shower” is used to describe a party whose primary purpose is to 
give gifts. The two most common types are a bridal shower, in which gifts are 
given to a woman who is going to get married, and a baby shower, in which 
gifts for the baby are given to a pregnant woman. These events are usually 
organized by the woman’s sisters or friends. 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
A general word for an informal social gathering is a “get-together” – that’s a 
casual event without an event schedule, and you don’t need to dress up.  
One type of get-together which is common in the U.S. is a potluck, in which 
each guest brings a dish to share with everyone. 
 
A potluck 
A banquet and a ball are more formal events. Food is served at a banquet, 
and there is dancing at a ball.  
 
 
          The place setting at a banquet                            a ball 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
A cocktail party is usually held in the early evening, and drinks and light 
refreshments are served. 
 
Some social events are held for a specific purpose – such as networking, 
making social connections for business or career opportunities. A fundraiser 
is an event whose purpose is to gather donations for a cause, charity, or non-
profit organization. 
Finally, a reunion is a gathering of group members who have been separated 
for some time – in the U.S., there are college reunions and high school 
reunions to re-encounter classmates after many years. 
You can read about a few more different types of parties and gatherings here: 
http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Party 
One thing you might see on party invitations is RSVP – that means you need to 
tell the host if you plan to attend the party or not. 
 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
Describing Social Habits 
Someone who is friendly to others can be described as warm, cordial, or 
welcoming. The opposite – someone who is unfriendly – is cold or 
standoffish. 
 
 
 
A person who loves social situations and gets energy from being with people 
is an extrovert – but a more common way to describe this type of person is to 
say they are outgoing. 
Someone who is outgoing is often a social butterfly – someone who has many 
different friends and goes from person to person and conversation to 
conversation like a butterfly visits different flowers. 
 
One idiom to describe someone who is the center of attention and makes 
parties fun and exciting is to say they are “the life of the party” – and a 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
“party animal” is someone who likes to go out to parties and clubs as often as 
possible. 
 
The opposite of an extrovert is an introvert – someone who prefers to spend 
time alone or with only a few close friends. More common words to describe 
this type of person are shy and reserved.  
 
Sometimes (though not always) introverts are socially awkward, meaning 
they are uncomfortable and a little bit strange in social interactions. A person 
who is an extreme introvert and who actively avoids the company of others 
can be called a loner. 
When someone who used to be shy begins to be more sociable and outgoing, 
we say the person has come out of his/her shell – making reference to the 
way a turtle pokes its head out of its shell to interact with the world. 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
Two types of person that no one wants to be are a wet blanket and party 
pooper. A “wet blanket” is someone whose attitude lessens the enjoyment of 
other people around them, or who discourages joy. A “party pooper” is 
someone whose words or actions ruin the fun or excitement for everyone else.

Lesson 9: Clothing & Fashion 
In this lesson, you’re going to learn three main vocabulary groups: words for 
various types of fabric, more advanced ways to describe the fit and form of 
clothing, and how to describe a person’s style. 
Fabrics 
Clothing can be made of various types of fabric – some are natural and others 
are synthetic (artificial): 
• cotton comes from a plant 
 
• silk is a very soft and luxurious fabric that comes from a worm  
 
 
• leather comes from the hide (skin) of an animal 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
 
• wool comes from sheep. The process of cutting the wool off the sheep is 
called “shearing.” 
 
• fur comes from animals – this is a fur coat 
 
• denim is the fabric used to make jeans 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
 
• lace is a fabric with decorative patterns 
 
• polyester, nylon, and spandex are synthetic fabrics. Polyester is used 
in many types of clothing and is often blended (mixed) with cotton; 
nylon is a strong and water-resistant material often used in jackets, 
tents, and backpacks; and spandex is an elastic material used in 
stretchy, close-fitting clothing. 
The design on a fabric is called the pattern. Some of the most common 
patterns are: 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
 
 
 
 
stripes 
 
 
 
 
plaid 
 
 
 
 
 
paisley 
 
 
polka dots  
 
 
floral 
Fit and Form 
You already know that clothing that is too small is tight, and clothing that is 
too big is loose – but now you’ll expand your vocabulary with some more 
descriptive words. 
Clothing that is extremely loose, with a lot of extra space, can be described as 
baggy. Clothing that follows the shape of your body more accurately, yet 
without being too tight, can be called tailored. And clothes that fit very close 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
to your body are form-fitting clothes. You can also say that the clothes fit you 
like a glove. 
Some people are too small or too large to fit into the typical sizes. Petite 
clothing is made for people who are short and slim, and plus-size clothing is 
for people who are larger than average. Maternity clothes are specially made 
for pregnant women. 
Let’s look more specifically at various styles of shirts and pants. 
Some common types of necklines for a shirt are: 
 
 
 
 
 
V-neck 
 
scoop neck 
 
 
 
 
 
 
crew neck  
turtleneck 
If a woman’s shirt exposes her cleavage (the space between her breasts), we 
can say it is low-cut.  
Both men and women can wear polo shirts – these shirts have a collar, but 
only two or three buttons – different from button-down shirts, which have 
buttons all the way down their front. Two styles that women can wear in the 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
summer are a halter top – that describes the style with a strap around the 
neck and an open back – and a tube top, which has no straps at all. 
 
 
 
 
 
polo shirt

How about different types of pants? There are cargo pants, which have large 
pockets on the legs. Capris are in between pants and shorts; they typically 
come to mid-calf. Leggings are skin-tight, and sweatpants are loose cotton 
pants often used for working out or relaxing. 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net

sweatpants 
Style 
Here are some words typically used to describe the style of clothing. 
Informal clothing for everyday wear is called casual, whereas clothes that are 
appropriate for “nicer” occasions – like going on a date or a job interview – are 
called dressy.  


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
The adjective sporty describes clothes that have an athletic style, and the 
word trendy describes clothes that are modern and fashionable. Two other 
words for “trendy” are chic and stylish.   
If someone is wearing revealing clothing, it means the clothes show a 
significant portion of their body. The opposite, conservative clothing which 
covers most of your body, is described as modest clothing. 
A person who has no fashion sense (the natural ability to choose nice-looking 
clothes) might be dressed in clothing that is out of style (considered 
unattractive and unpopular nowadays) or that is not flattering – that means it 
doesn’t look good on their body.  
This person can hire a personal shopper who can help them revise their 
wardrobe – a word that can refer to all the clothing a person owns. The 
personal shopper can help you put together some nice outfits (the word 
“outfit” refers to the total combination of all the clothing and accessories you 
are wearing).

Lesson 10: Movie Reviews 
Today you’ll learn vocabulary for praising and criticizing various aspects of 
films. The worksheet for this lesson will review the major movie genres 
(types of movies) and help you practice skimming – reading fast. 
Plot / Dialogue 
The plot is the story; the sequence of events in the movie. The plot unfolds in 
a series of scenes - each scene is a moment in a particular time/place - and 
the high point of the movie, or the moment of highest-intensity action, is 
called the climax. 
In some movies, the story moves very fast - in this case, you can describe the 
movie as fast-paced (the opposite being slow-paced or sluggish). Some 
movies start out fast and exciting, but the story slows down and gets boring in 
the middle or end. In this case, we say the movie started to drag (slow down) 
or that it fizzled out (had a promising beginning, but a disappointing ending). 
If the movie holds your attention very well from beginning to end, you can say 
it was gripping. 
One common technique in movies is to have a twist in the plot - that means a 
sudden, unexpected, surprising turn of events in the story. On the other hand, 
if a movie is predictable, that means you can guess exactly what is going to 
happen next.  
If the director prepares just the right mixture of emotion, conflict, and 
resolution, the movie is described as touching or moving (that means it 
deeply emotionally affects you). Sometimes a particularly uplifting (positive) 
movie is called "a feel-good movie." But if the movie has excessive 
sentimentality, then it is called sappy. 
Trying to communicate a moral lesson through the movie can also be hit-or-
miss. If done effectively, the movie is described as powerful or thought-


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
provoking. But if the director tries to drive home his point too hard, then the 
movie can be called "preachy." 
Within the story, we have dialogue (the direct words/conversations of the 
characters) and you can also comment on this aspect when reviewing a movie. 
If the dialogue is extremely funny, you can describe it as hilarious. If it is 
funny, but in a more subtle, clever way, you can say it is witty. On the negative 
side, dialogue that is boring can be described as uninspired. If the language is 
vulgar or offensive, then you can say it is crude. 
Cast / Characters 
The second major element of a movie is its cast - this word refers to the group 
of actors and actresses who participate in the movie. The main character in 
the story is sometimes called the protagonist, and the actor/actress who 
plays this character is said to have the leading role or the lead.  
In some movies - particularly action movies that feature a strong main 
character or hero - the hero has a "sidekick" - that's like an assistant who 
helps him/her during the adventures. The evil character or "bad guy" of the 
story is called the villain. 
 
We can describe the actors’ performance in the movie by saying that the 
acting was either "strong" or "weak." For an especially good job by a 
particular actor/actress, you can say that he/she gave a brilliant or riveting 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
performance. “Brilliant,” in this case, means excellent - and “riveting” means 
that it was so fascinating that you couldn't look away. 
If the acting was not very natural, you can say that the acting was wooden. 
Another word used to criticize a character in a movie is describing him/her as 
"one-dimensional" – that means the personality of their character had no 
complexity or detail.  
Setting / Stunts / Soundtrack 
Finally, we have the visual and audio elements of the film. The setting refers 
to both the location and the time period of the story. To describe the setting, 
we typically say, "The film is set in... [18th-century Japan]" or "The story takes 
place in... [modern-day New York City]."  
The soundtrack is the music used in the film. Sometimes it consists of songs 
that already exist, and other times it is composed specifically for the movie. 
Stunts are amazing acrobatic or dangerous movements performed in fight 
and action sequences. Many actors/actresses have a "stunt double" - a 
professionally-trained person who looks like him/her, who performs these 
difficult and dangerous actions. This person is called a stunt man or a stunt 
woman. Nowadays, movie producers can also use computers to create special 
effects. 
 
If the visual aspects of the movie are impressive, we can describe them as 
stunning or spectacular. Sometimes the special effects are a little TOO 
exaggerated, and in this case they are described as over-the-top. If the quality 
of the special effects was poor, you can describe them as cheap (or cheap-
looking) or shoddy. 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
Overall Success / Failure of a Movie 
If a movie was extremely popular and sold an enormous number of tickets, it 
is called a blockbuster or a hit. To say that the quality of a movie is excellent 
(without commenting on its popularity), you can call it a masterpiece - and a 
movie that has been consistently enjoyed by many people over many years is 
considered a classic.  
By contrast, if a movie had a lot of buzz or hype (publicity aiming to increase 
the public’s excitement), but turned out to be terrible, you can describe it as a 
disaster or a flop.

Lesson 10 Exercise: Skimming  
One essential reading skill that is seldom practiced is skimming – the ability to read 
quickly to get a basic overview of the text. Instead of reading word by word, you just 
“look over” the text very fast. 
Below are 11 descriptions of the major movie genres. Try to skim – not read – and 
match each paragraph with the name of the genre in less than 3 minutes. 
Genres: 
• Action / Adventure  
• Children's / Family 
• Comedy 
• Documentary 
• Drama 
• Fantasy 
• Horror 
• Suspense / Thriller 
• Romance 
• Sci-fi 
• War 
1. ______________________________ 
A genre characterized by futuristic elements and advanced technology, often 
involving space exploration. Some examples of films within this category involve the 
invasion of the planet by aliens; others explore how "science gone wrong" can result 
in a battle of man versus technology. These movies feature the heavy use of special 
effects. 
2. ______________________________ 
A type of historical fiction in which an armed conflict is the backdrop for the story. 
Some movies of this type focus on the battles and on political and ideological topics 
related to the combat. In others, the main story has nothing to do with combat; 
instead, they explore how the violent setting affects the main characters' lives.  


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
3. ______________________________ 
Another large genre, this type of film keeps viewers on the edge of their seats 
wondering what will happen next. There is often a mystery to be solved or a 
criminal to be caught, and in the end the good guys typically win and life goes back 
to normal. These films frequently use music (or silence) and camera angles to 
preserve moments of tension until a sudden outburst of action or violence, which 
makes you jump. 
4. ______________________________ 
Designed to be appropriate for young audiences, these films are often animated and 
usually consist of comedies or adventures that involve animals, imaginary beings, 
and creative and colorful fantasy worlds. Free of violence, sexuality, or offensive 
language, these films aim to stimulate the imagination and teach helpful lessons 
through the story. 
5. ______________________________ 
Designed to frighten or shock the viewer with scary stories and disturbing images, 
these films often feature zombies, evil spirits, horrible creatures, perverse people, or 
unknown dangers. It is common for them to display explicit gore and other 
nightmare-inducing visuals. 
6. ______________________________ 
In this type of film, one or more heroes must face a series of challenges as they aim 
to solve a crisis or defeat a villain. In the course of the story, the hero is usually 
involved in physical fights, acrobatic stunts, and exciting combat and chase scenes. 
The focus of these films is on adrenaline, excitement and danger; not as much 
emphasis is given to the storyline or character development. 
7. ______________________________ 
In this type of film, the absurdity of the characters, dialogue, and scenes is often 
exaggerated for the sake of entertainment – the primary goal is to make you laugh. 
Most of these movies simply aim to make the viewer feel better about the 
ridiculousness of life without delving into more profound topics; however, they may 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
also use humor to provide commentary about a particular aspect of society or 
culture. 
8. ______________________________ 
The main storyline of these films focuses on a relationship between two (or more) 
characters who are attracted to each other. They must then navigate the obstacles 
that make it difficult for them to stay together. Films of this type can be on the light-
hearted and funny side, or have a more serious tone. 
9. ______________________________ 
This category, which explores emotions and interpersonal relationships, is one of 
the broadest cinematic genres. These films often involve one or more characters 
who are at a crossroads in their lives, exploring the conflicts and realizations that 
occur as events unfold. They require excellent acting and skillful character 
development to be moving for the audience. 
10. ______________________________ 
This is a broad category of nonfiction films providing factual information about a 
person or event. A film of this type may describe a well-researched historical event, 
trace the life trajectory of an intriguing person, or explore a scientific or cultural 
phenomenon. Although a purely factual film may sound rather dry, these movies 
often make use of dramatic elements and storytelling techniques in order to present 
the information in an engaging and memorable way. 
11. ______________________________ 
This type of film is set in an imaginary world with magical or supernatural 
characters such as gods, fairies, angels, giants, elves, and other non-human beings. 
These imaginary universes often have their own histories and laws of nature, where 
magic and super-powers are possible. 
(Answers at the end of this document) 
There are also many "sub-genres" – smaller categories within the main ones. For 
example, the category of “action movies” includes "martial arts" movies and 
"superhero" movies. A movie that is classified as “drama” can be a "political drama," 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
"medical drama," or "courtroom drama," among others. For an extensive listing of 
all movie genres and sub-genres, click here: http://www.allmovie.com/genre/all

Lesson 11: Books & Writing 
Do you like to read? Today’s lesson is all about describing books: specific 
categories of books as well as vocabulary words for commenting on the 
positive and negative points of the writing. 
Book Genres 
Remember the word “genre” from yesterday’s lesson on movies? It means a 
type or category. Many of the same genres from movies also apply to books, 
like science fiction, thriller, and mystery. Here are a few more specific literary 
genres: 
• A biography is the story of a person’s life. If that person wrote the book 
about themselves, then it’s called an autobiography. 
• A memoir is similar to an autobiography in that the author recounts 
his/her experiences, but it may focus on one specific time period rather 
than the entire lifetime. Memoirs tend to have a more personal and 
emotional tone, while an autobiography tends to be factual and 
chronological. 
• A chronicle is a detailed non-fiction account of historical events, 
focusing on facts without commentary from the author. 
• An anthology is a collection of pieces (like short stories, poems, or 
plays) in a single book. 
• A novel is a long fictional story. 
• A self-help book teaches you how to improve yourself and your life. 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
• A satire is a work that makes fun of 
human society or an institution, often 
pointing out its flaws through 
exaggeration and humor. Political 
cartoons are examples of satire. 
 
Sometimes a book tells the untold story of 
a particular person or event – meaning a 
story that has never been revealed to the public. If a story is a first-hand 
account, that means it’s written by someone who experienced the situation 
personally. 
Finally, if a book is one of the most popular and many people have bought it, it 
is called a bestseller. 
People in the Writing Industry 
A person who writes books can be called an author or a writer. We also have 
words for writers of more specific types: 
• Someone who writes novels is a novelist.  
• Someone who writes poetry is a poet. 
• Someone who writes plays is a playwright. 
 
The company that produces and 
publishes books is called the 
publisher or publishing house. The 
publisher often has a team of editors 
to help improve the books and 
proofreaders to check for mistakes. 
 
 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
Book Reviews: Positive and Negative 
If a book was exciting and interesting, you can call it a page-turner – like you 
couldn’t stop reading! Other ways to say a book held your attention are to call 
it riveting or compelling and to say, “I couldn’t put it down.” 
You can also comment on the way the book made you feel: 
• A book that awoke your curiosity and interest is intriguing 
• A book that is happy and not too serious is lighthearted 
• A book that deeply emotionally affects you (often in a bittersweet way) 
is poignant 
• A book that is delightful and charming is enchanting 
• A book that is deep (not superficial) is profound 
 
 
How about the writing itself? One word you’ll often see in book reviews is 
prose – that simply means normal writing, not poetry. If the author’s prose is 
vivid, it means it was colorful and lively. Prose that is lyrical means it is 
beautiful to read or listen to. Writing that is succinct is clear and direct, with 
few extra words. If you don’t want to be specific, you can simply say the book 
was masterfully written. 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
Finally, a few words used for complimenting non-fiction books are: 
• insightful: had a lot of interesting ideas and perspectives 
• comprehensive: covering the topic completely, not missing anything 
• nuanced: expressing subtle differences and details 
• an in-depth analysis: a thorough, well-done study and explanation 
 
Here are some words for commenting on the book’s shortcomings – meaning 
flaws, or places where it wasn’t as good as it could have been. 
If the book had a lot of jargon, it had lots of technical terms that were not easy 
to understand. Describing writing as wordy means it had too many 
unnecessary words, and describing writing as flowery means it had an 
exaggerated number of “beautiful” words.  
Sometimes the author repeats the same ideas or phrases too often – in this 
case, you can describe the writing as repetitive. If the writing is boring and 
lacks variety, then it is monotonous or tedious.  
 
If the plot of a book was complicated and hard to follow, you can say it was 
disjointed. Sometimes, the end of a book is difficult to believe based on what 
happened earlier in the story – in this case, the ending was implausible. 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
When criticizing a non-fiction book, you can say that the author was biased – 
meaning his/her personal opinions interfere with the presentation of the 
facts. If the author has left out important points, then he has made some 
omissions. And if the author’s points are very general, not specific and not 
clearly expressed, then they are vague. 
Whenever you write a book or movie review, be careful to avoid spoilers – 
telling people who haven’t read the book yet about the surprise events or the 
ending of the story!

criptions.pdf  
• http://www.soquelhs.net/library/net%20links/tone_words.pdf

Lesson 12: Cradle to Grave 
Pregnancy & Birth 
The very first moment of pregnancy is conception – when the man’s sperm 
fertilizes the woman’s egg.  
 
The baby then begins growing in the mother’s uterus, which is more 
commonly called her womb – connected to the mother through the umbilical 
cord. 
 
When a couple is having difficulty conceiving, that is called infertility. There 
are a few different treatments, including fertility-enhancing drugs and IVF – in 
vitro fertilization – where the sperm and egg are combined outside the 
woman’s body and then implanted in her uterus. 
A pregnant woman may experience morning sickness and cravings – intense 
desires for particular foods. The nine months of a normal pregnancy are 
divided into three periods of three months each, called trimesters. One of the 
exams commonly performed during pregnancy is an ultrasound.  


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
 
If a baby is born much earlier than the due date (the date expected), then it is 
premature (premature babies are sometimes called “preemies”).  
 
Any significant problems during the pregnancy are referred to as 
complications, and if the baby dies in the middle of the pregnancy, this is a 
miscarriage – although in everyday English it’s more common to say the 
woman “lost the baby/pregnancy.” In some countries, a woman can have an 
abortion – choose to terminate the pregnancy and not let the baby live. 
The work of giving birth is called labor, and during labor the woman will 
experience strong contractions. To relieve the pain, she can have an epidural 
– that’s an injection in her back. There are two methods of delivering a baby – 
a vaginal birth through the vagina, and a C-section in which the mother’s 
stomach is cut open and the baby is removed. 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
After the birth, the mother can breastfeed the baby or use formula, which is 
a manufactured mixture of milk and nutrients.  
 
 
 
breastfeeding 
 
 
 
using formula 
And the place where a newborn baby sleeps is called a cradle or bassinet. 
 
Death 
Let’s jump to the other end of the life cycle – death. After a person dies, 
his/her body is usually called a “body” if being referred to by people who 
know and love the person. The word corpse also means a dead body, but it’s 
more distant, less personal. 
If a corpse is found in the woods, for example, and no one knows how the 
person died, the police will do an autopsy – an investigation to find the cause 
of death. A place where dead bodies are kept and preserved until they are 
identified and arrangements can be made is called a morgue or mortuary.  


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
 
What’s done with the body after a person dies? One option is being buried 
inside a coffin/casket, in a cemetery with a tombstone or headstone to 
mark the spot. The place where someone is buried is called a grave. 
 
 
coffin/casket 
 
 
 
tombstones/headstones 
An alternative is to have the body cremated (the body burned in a very hot 
fire) and have the ashes (the remains after cremation) either scattered 
outdoors or kept by the family in an urn. 
 
 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
A ceremony to mark someone’s death is called a funeral. At a funeral, a close 
friend or family member may give a eulogy – a speech praising the person 
who has died and sharing some happy memories. An obituary is often 
published in the local newspaper, giving a brief overview of the life of the 
deceased. 
Another funeral tradition in the U.S. is a wake or viewing, which is a time 
when family and friends can look at the body on display in the coffin and pay 
their respects. A memorial service may also be held – this is a ceremony to 
remember the person’s life, but the coffin/casket with the body is not present. 
When dealing with death, it’s important to be sensitive to the feelings of 
people who are grieving or mourning (feeling extremely sad because of a 
loss). A gentler way to say “died” is “passed away,” for example: “I heard your 
grandfather passed away last week. I’m so sorry for your loss.” 
This last phrase is common in spoken English; in written English we can use 
more formal phrases like “My heartfelt condolences to you and your family” 
and “I’d like to express my deepest sympathies for your loss.” (More phrases 
here: http://www.quickcondolence.com/)

Lesson 13: Appearance & Personal 
Care 
Hair 
A small haircut is called a trim. Anyone with long hair should get a trim 
regularly in order to get rid of split ends (when the end of each strand of hair 
divides in two). 
To change the color of your hair, you can dye it a different color. Sometimes 
people dye only a few small pieces of hair – this is called getting highlights. 
 
highlights 
What about some typical hairstyles? 
 
 
 
 
 
afro  
 
 
bangs 
 
 
an updo 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
 
 
 
 
 
 
layers 
 
 
braid 
 
 
 
 
 
 
a ponytail  
 
spiked 
 
 
dreadlocks 
An afro is a large, curly style often used by people of African descent. Bangs 
are short pieces of hair that cover your forehead. An updo is any style in 
which the hair is pinned up on top of the head; updos are often used for 
formal events.  
Hair with layers has pieces of different lengths. A braid is created by weaving 
three sections of hair together, and a ponytail is simply holding the hair 
together with an elastic band. You can use hair gel to make your hair spiked, 
and dreadlocks are a hairstyle in which the hair is twisted into matted 
sections. 
If someone has lost their hair, they can use a toupee or a wig. The difference 
is that a toupee covers a bald spot and is usually used by men; a wig is a 
complete hair replacement and is usually used by women. 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
 
 
The hair that grows on your body is called “body hair,” and there are several 
different ways to remove it: 
• shave with a razor – men usually do this to their faces 
 
• pluck hairs with tweezers – women often do this to their eyebrows 
 
• wax – remove the hair by applying hot wax, letting it cool, then ripping 
it off 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
 
• laser hair removal – permanent or semi-permanent hair removal 
 
Skin 
Teenagers often have a skin problem called acne, in which red bumps called 
pimples appear on the face. When you get older, the skin problems change – 
you get wrinkles (lines) and age spots (small dark areas) instead. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
acne  
 
 
 
wrinkles 
These small brown marks on the face are called freckles, and a single dark 
spot which can be anywhere on the body is called a mole.  
 
 
 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
Makeup can help hide imperfections of the skin, and there’s also a spa 
treatment called a facial in which a special cream mask is put on the face to 
heal and help the skin. For serious problems, you can see a doctor specializing 
in the skin, called a dermatologist. 
 
 
makeup  
 
 
 
a facial 
Click here for more makeup/cosmetics vocabulary 
 
Body 
Your idea and opinion of how your body looks and 
how attractive you are is called your body image. If 
you’re not satisfied with your body, this can be 
damaging to your self-esteem – your general feeling 
about yourself. 
Women often worry about their figure – that’s a 
general word for the shape of your body – and men 
tend to be concerned with their physique – the 
proportions of your body, especially the muscles. 
Men who want to get more muscular can lift 
weights or take supplements in an attempt to “bulk up” – become more 
muscular. 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
 
 
lifting weights  
 
supplements 
To lose weight, the best strategy is proper nutrition and exercise – but 
unfortunately some people develop eating disorders like anorexia (eating 
extremely little food and not enough nutrients) and bulimia (vomiting your 
food immediately after eating it). 
Another way to change the appearance of your body is to get plastic surgery 
or cosmetic surgery. Some of the most common types are: 
• breast implants – to make the breasts bigger 
• liposuction – surgically removing fat from inside the body 
• a tummy tuck – smoothing and stretching the skin of the stomach 
• a facelift – removes wrinkles and makes the face look younger 
• a nose job – changing the shape of the nose

Lesson 14: Character & Behavior 
Today we’re going to learn positive and negative character traits using the 
Chinese zodiac – that’s a form of astrology, the belief that the movement of the 
stars and planets can affect people and events on earth. 
As you go through the lesson, think about which traits describe you and which 
ones don't. 
Year of the Rat: 1948, 1960, 1972, 1984, 1996 
 
Strengths: People born in the year of the rat are diligent (that means hard-
working) and tend to be wealthy (rich). They are personable (that means 
friendly and popular, with a good social life) and sensible (they have a good 
understanding of practical situations). 
Weaknesses: They tend to be greedy (that means desiring too much money 
and resources) and selfish (meaning they only care about themselves) as well 
as stubborn (meaning they are firm in their beliefs and not easily influenced 
by others). 
Year of the Ox: 1949, 1961, 1973, 1985, 1997 
Strengths: People born in these years are patient and cautious (meaning they 
are careful and don’t like to take risks). They are also contemplative, 
meaning they think a lot before taking action or making a decision, and 
tender-hearted (meaning compassionate – they care about other people). 
Weaknesses: They are poor communicators and not especially charming 
(charming means a person who is enchanting and interesting, who captures 
your attention) – so some might call them boring. 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
Year of the Tiger: 1950, 1962, 1974, 1986, 1998 
Strengths: Tigers are considered tolerant (meaning they accept other people 
who are different without judging or criticizing them) and brave (which 
means courageous, without fear). 
Weaknesses: They can be rash (meaning they act without thinking, 
sometimes with disastrous results) and short-tempered, meaning they get 
angry easily. 
Year of the Rabbit: 1951, 1963, 1975, 1987, 1999 
Strengths: People born in the year of the rabbit are humble (that means not 
arrogant) and are known for being hospitable (welcoming people into their 
homes). 
Weaknesses: Rabbits can be so reserved (meaning they are timid, not 
ambitious) that they may miss out on some opportunities. They often “have 
their heads in the clouds” – meaning they like to dream and escape reality. 
Year of the Dragon: 1952, 1964, 1976, 1988, 2000 
Strengths: Dragons are lively and energetic (both of these words mean they 
have a lot of energy), and optimistic (meaning they focus on the positive). 
They are not intimidated by difficulties. 
Weaknesses: A tendency to be arrogant (having too high an opinion of 
yourself) and impatient, as well as moody (that means their emotions change 
unpredictably). 
Year of the Snake: 1953, 1965, 1977, 1989, 2001 
Strengths: Snakes are considered wise (meaning they have profound 
knowledge and understanding), passionate (meaning they put a lot of 
emotion into their interests and activities), and determined (meaning they 
are strongly motivated to accomplish their goals).  
Weaknesses: They are fickle (indecisive, can’t commit to things for the long-
term) and headstrong – meaning they rely strongly on themselves, without 
listening to or considering other people’s opinions. 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
Year of the Horse: 1954, 1966, 1978, 1990, 2002 
Strengths: People born in the year of the horse are great communicators and 
love to be in the spotlight (that means they enjoy having everyone’s attention 
focused on them). They are also cheerful (with a consistently happy attitude) 
and perceptive (meaning they notice small details). 
Weaknesses: They are superficial (meaning they only focus on the outer 
appearance) as well as hot-blooded (easily excited or angered). 
Year of the Sheep: 1955, 1967, 1979, 1991, 2003 
Strengths: People born in these years are diplomatic (meaning polite and 
respectful of other people) and kind (that means nice or pleasant to others), 
with a special sensitivity to art, beauty, and faith. 
Weaknesses: Sheep tend to be anxious (meaning they worry too much), shy 
(too quiet, not good in social situations), and over-sensitive (meaning their 
feelings are easily hurt). 
Year of the Monkey: 1956, 1968, 1980, 1992, 2004 
Strengths: Monkeys are innovative (meaning creative and good at solving 
problems), self-assured (meaning confident), and versatile (meaning they 
have many different abilities and adapt well to change). 
Weaknesses: They are sometimes seen as eccentric (a little bit strange), with 
a tendency to look down on others (that means view other people as 
inferior). 
Year of the Rooster: 1957, 1969, 1981, 1993, 2005 
Strengths: Roosters are bright (smart, intelligent) and capable (lots of 
abilities and potential) as well as punctual (they arrive on time). 
Weaknesses: Because of their high self-confidence, roosters can be narrow-
minded (meaning they believe they are always right, and don’t want to listen 
to other possibilities) and vain (concerned about their appearance). 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
Year of the Dog: 1958, 1970, 1982, 1994, 2006 
Strengths: The dog is considered “man’s best friend,” and people born in 
these years are said to be straightforward (honest, transparent, with no lies 
or hidden aspects) and courageous, making them good leaders. 
Weaknesses: Their weaknesses include being irritable (easily annoyed) and 
cynical (meaning they frequently criticize and disapprove of things). 
Year of the Pig: 1959, 1971, 1983, 1995, 2007 
Strengths: People born in the year of the pig are sincere (honest, genuine) 
and loyal (dedicated to their relationships and commitments). 
Weaknesses: Pigs are often naïve (that means they trust people too easily), 
and can sometimes be impulsive (making spontaneous decisions without 
enough thought or planning).

Lesson 15: Relationships 
Getting Together 
Let’s begin with friendship. If a man and a woman have a platonic 
relationship, it means they are only friends; there is no romantic relationship.  
Maybe they just didn’t have a spark or 
chemistry – both these words are used to 
describe romantic connection that feels 
exciting and natural. 
Sometimes a person develops a crush on 
one of their friends – if you have a crush on 
someone, it means you have secret romantic 
feelings for that person. 
Some couples get together through a blind date – that’s when they didn’t 
know each other before the date. A mutual friend often “sets up” the blind 
date. 
Casual Relationships 
A brief romantic or sexual relationship that’s not serious is called a fling. A 
fling can last anywhere from a couple weeks to a few months. Even shorter 
than a fling is a one-night stand – having just one night of sex with someone. 
It’s common to use the expression “hook up” for an intimate encounter. 
Sometimes hooking up leads to the beginning of a relationship, and other 
times it’s just for fun. There’s also a type of relationship called friends with 
benefits – two friends who have sex with each other because they enjoy it, but 
they don’t have a commitment or romantic relationship. 
Someone who has casual sex with a lot of different people can be described as 
promiscuous. Another expression for having sex with many partners is 
sleeping around.  


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
Anyone who does this should be careful to use contraceptives (devices or 
drugs to prevent pregnancy) and condoms to prevent disease. 
 
  
   
 
 
contraceptives (birth control pills) and a condom 
Serious Relationships 
There are a number of ways to say that two people are in a committed 
relationship. You can say that he/she is taken or that the two of them are an 
item. When two people decide to maintain their relationship even though 
they live in different places, this is called a long-distance relationship. 
Two people who want to spend every 
minute of the day together can be described 
as inseparable. Some couples feel they are 
soul mates – connected to each other on the 
deepest level. When you want to comment 
that two people in a relationship are very 
compatible, you can say they’re a match 
made in heaven. 
Occasionally, two people have a relationship that seems completely wonderful 
and perfect, without any problems – this is called a fairy tale romance 
because it seems like a fantasy story! 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
 
There are a few expressions regarding marriage – when a man asks a woman 
to marry him, this is called proposing or more informally popping the 
question – and some idioms for the act of getting married are getting 
hitched and tying the knot.  
 
 
an engagement ring 
During the wedding ceremony, the couple make vows to each other – a vow is 
a very strong, very serious promise. 
 
Making vows (yes, this is me!) 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
Ending a Relationship 
If a couple breaks up or splits up, it means they separate. Sometimes the 
decision to break up is mutual – meaning both partners agree that it’s best to 
end the relationship. 
But if one person dumped the other, then it was only one 
person’s decision to end things, even though the other 
person wanted to continue. A person who gets dumped is 
often heartbroken – extremely sad. 
Relationship Habits 
Every relationship has its ups and downs (its good moments and bad 
moments), but here are some habits that can make a big difference. 
When getting into a new relationship, it’s important to recognize and deal 
with any baggage – that’s bad or complicated romantic experience in the past, 
which ends up having a negative effect on the new relationship. If the 
relationship consistently has problems, it can be described as a rocky or 
stormy relationship. 
 
 
A "rocky" or "stormy" relationship is full of conflict 
Some couples have a whirlwind romance – that’s a relationship that 
progresses extremely quickly to marriage. This sometimes works out – but 
often when a person is desperate to find a partner, they can rush the romance 
and end up ignoring red flags – those are signs of possible danger or 


 
 
- EspressoEnglish.net 
incompatibility in the relationship. Their partner might even turn out to be 
abusive – someone who physically, verbally, or emotionally injures another 
person. 
One of the secrets to a happy and healthy relationship is compromise – 
finding a fair solution in the middle of two different opinions, desires, or 
directions. After all, you won’t always see eye to eye (agree with each other 
or understand each other’s perspectives).  
Another expression for compromise is “give and take” – both partners need 
to work together, sometimes sacrificing their own wants, to preserve 
harmony in the relationship.
